findings.summary: Cargo.toml is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: "High priority" is never checked the way Athena actually reads it.
findings.evidence: `Athena::queue(&self, text)` (crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs:550) takes no priority argument; it stores only the request text. Priority comes from a `Priority:` line, which plan.rs reads (plan.rs:73). The plan's "priority verified in Records" is vague: the request record holds text only, so a check that the text contains "Priority: high" never exercises the code that turns it into a priority. Fix: In the cadence test, pass the queued request text through plan.rs's priority parser (the function documented at plan.rs:73) and assert `Priority::High`. Or assert on the `athena plan` entry for the job.

findings.summary: `athena plan` may refuse the queued requests because they have no acceptance bullets.
findings.evidence: System facts (Request format): without acceptance bullets or a reading's criteria, an item is refused for design or code. The plan says what the structural-pass and design-review texts contain, but neither includes acceptance bullets. Fix: Give both request texts acceptance bullets (lines starting with `-`). Have the criterion-6 test check that the design-review text produces a plan entry that `athena plan` does not refuse.

findings.summary: Other commits with an Athena-Job trailer on main can inflate the landing count.
findings.evidence: Many writers add an Athena-Job trailer: reading.rs:582/619/682, manage.rs:134/172, proposals.rs:659, work_decisions.rs:332, and the bootstrap commits (`Athena-Job: bootstrap`). Before the records cutover, records commits sit on main; land.rs:439 has a test fixture with "Records\n\nAthena-Job: jb". Counting every trailer commit would shift both the cadence and the 7-day churn. Fix: Count a landing only when the commit's trailers carry both Athena-Job and Athena-Verified-Content, which is how `landed_commit` at gh.rs:1287 identifies one. Or skip the `bootstrap` job and records-only commits. Add a test fixture with a records-only trailer commit and assert it is not counted.
findings.location: Decision 2 (landing = first-parent commit with an Athena-Job trailer)

findings.summary: In one run both hooks may fire; the test should prove that queues nothing twice.
findings.evidence: run.rs:152 calls `note_finished` after a job finishes, and `Athena::land_pr` (gh.rs:2575-2590) runs its own hook after `resync_onto_merge` and the Pages watch. The plan argues the double firing is idempotent but does not test it. Fix: Add a test that runs both hooks for one landing and asserts that exactly one structural-pass request is queued and that no extra baseline or review is written.

summary: I checked the plan by reading the code; I did not run anything. Every location the plan names exists in the base. `Athena::land_pr` (gh.rs:2455) calls `resync_onto_merge` (gh.rs:2575) and then watches the Pages deploy (gh.rs:2577-2590), so a hook after both is well placed. `note_finished` (steward.rs:98) returns early for nested runs, so the plan's choice to put the hook before that return is correct. The trailer name Athena-Job is confirmed. Cargo.lock already pins syn 2.0.119 and proc-macro2 1.0.107, and the root Cargo.toml has `[workspace.dependencies]`. That makes the extra Cargo.toml edit necessary; I weighed Athena's own finding about it as justified. Each criterion has a demonstration that would fail without the behavior. The 9-versus-10 landing test, the reload into a fresh state directory and the hook-removal checks are all sound. There are four minor findings: (1) the high-priority check should go through the plan.rs priority parser; (2) the queued request texts need acceptance bullets or `athena plan` may refuse them; (3) counting every commit with an Athena-Job trailer can inflate the landing count; (4) one landing that fires both hooks should be tested to queue only once. None is a blocker or major, so I accept.
